pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Blaise—a place where EVERYONE is welcome, valued, and celebrated.
As a proud Church of England school, our vision and values guide everything we do. Rooted in Christian principles, we create a nurturing and inclusive environment where everyone—regardless of their faith, background, or worldview—feels supported and valued as part of our community.
At the heart of our school is our vision: exploring and achieving as we grow together. More than just a place to learn, St Blaise is a supportive family where we all grow, explore, and achieve together.
We take pride in our beautiful school grounds, sensory spaces, and science garden, which offer children unique ways to connect with nature, discover their world, and find moments of inspiration and calm. These spaces are designed to support learning, wellbeing, and spirituality.
To learn more, we warmly encourage you to explore our website or visit us to experience the unique and welcoming community at St Blaise.

pageCache.pageTitle: Child Absence & Attendance – St Blaise Primary School
pageCache.text:
Times of the school day
Attendance and Absence
At St Blaise, every child is valued and plays an important part in our school community. To explore, achieve, and grow together, we believe it’s essential that children are in school, learning and sharing experiences each day. Good attendance helps children build confidence, make progress, and feel fully part of school life.
Punctuality and Lateness
Being on time is an important life skill and helps children start the day calmly and ready to learn. We understand there are times when lateness cannot be avoided — if this happens, please let us know. If your child arrives after the register has closed, they should come to the school office to be signed in.
If your child is often late, we’ll work with you to understand any difficulties and offer support so that mornings can run more smoothly.
Illness and Absence
If your child is unwell, please contact the school by 9:00am on the first day of absence by calling 01235 831368 (you can leave a message on the absence line). Please let us know how long you think your child might be away.
If we haven’t heard from you, we’ll get in touch to make sure your child is safe and accounted for. We need to log the reasons for absence, so please let us know as soon as possible why your child cannot attend.
Sickness Guidelines
To help prevent the spread of illness, children who have had vomiting or diarrhoea should remain at home until 48 hours after their last symptoms and until they are feeling well enough to return. For other conditions and illnesses, please refer to the NHS guidance on “Is my child too ill for school?” or ring the school office — we can help you decide what’s best.
If your child becomes unwell during the school day, we’ll contact you or another named adult to collect them.
Medical Appointments
Where possible, please arrange medical or dental appointments outside school hours. If that’s not possible, please email the office to let us know in advance and collect your child from the main entrance.
Authorised Absence
Absences can be authorised for the following reasons:
Medical appointments or illness
Religious observance
Approved sporting or educational activities
We are unable to authorise absences for other reasons, even if they seem important, unless they meet the criteria for exceptional circumstances.
Family Holidays
Government guidance means schools cannot authorise term-time holidays except in exceptional circumstances. If you believe this applies, please complete an Exceptional Leave of Absence form.
For further information please read the School’s Attendance Policy and Attendance strategy on the policies page.
For details about Emergency School Closure please read the following information Emergency School Closure

Worship at St Blaise
Worship is a treasured part of our school day, offering us a moment of stillness and calm amidst the busy routine. It’s a time when we come together as a whole school community to think, reflect, and share, creating a space that fosters connection and unity.
As a Christian school, our worship celebrates and promotes our core Christian values, while also respecting and embracing all faiths and worldviews to ensure everyone feels included and valued.
It is a statutory responsibility for all schools to provide pupils with the opportunity to take part in a daily act of worship. As parents, you have the right to withdraw your child from acts of worship or Religious Education lessons. Should you wish to do so, we ask that you speak to Becky Costello first and encourage you to take the time to attend an act of worship and read the Collective Worship in Church of England Schools Inclusive Invitational Inspiring guidance document, and our school’s collective worship policy before making a decision.
Sharing Worship
Parents, family, and friends are warmly invited to join us for special assemblies and services. Our celebration assemblies, held on Fridays at 9am, are a joyful celebration of the success and achievements of all children, and parents are always welcome. You can find the dates for these and other events in our newsletter and on the school website calendar.
Our School Prayer
We love beginning our worship with our heartfelt school prayer, which reflects our shared values and aspirations:
Heavenly Father, You planted us like seed ready to blossom. As we grow, help us to be rooted in your love, Surrounded by kindness and strengthened by one another. Help us to be unique, beautiful trees that flourish in your name. Amen
Lunchtime Grace
Lunchtime at St Blaise is a joyful occasion filled with gratitude and community spirit. Grace is led by the children, who often sing with enthusiasm and joy, reminding us to be thankful for the delicious food we share. Worship leaders take turns to express their thanks in unique ways, making this a special and vibrant part of the day.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information & Report – St Blaise Primary School
pageCache.text:
At Saint Blaise, we are deeply committed to being an inclusive school, where every member of our community is supported and valued. We strive to ensure that all pupils, staff, and families experience equality, equity, diversity, and inclusion in every aspect of school life.
Our dedicated staff team works closely with parents and carers to provide the best possible support for pupils with specific needs. These needs may relate to learning, behaviour, physical difficulties, global delay, or autism. Through collaboration and understanding, we aim to create an environment where every child can thrive and reach their full potential.
This team approach is led by Gaby Sandford, the school SENCO (Special Educational Needs Coordinator), who works tirelessly to ensure our school community is inclusive, compassionate, and supportive.
Please read our SEND Information report to find out more; you will find the answers to the following questions:
You can also refer to the following one-page documents regarding our 1:1 support provision and key points of contact.
You may also be interested in reviewing the SEND Policy, which is available on our policies page. The Inclusion Policy, Accessibility Policy and Plan, as well as the More and Most Able Policy, can also be found there.
Attached are the Department for Education (DfE) Parent and Carer Guide DfE Parent and Carer SEND Guide and the Oxfordshire Support Guide SEND-Support-Guidance for Oxfordshire

Every school is required to have a Governing Board: our governing board is made up of volunteers from the local community, parents, the Headteacher and a staff member. Together we have a collective responsibility for making sure that all children in our school receive the best education possible in a safe, caring and as a Church of England primary school, Christian environment. The Headteacher is responsible for the day-to-day management of the school. The Governing Board is strategic, which means that we plan for the future and consider how the school can achieve its targets and aspirations. An overview of St Blaise Strategic plans can be found here
The school has built its good reputation for being caring, friendly and supportive of every child and family. Our school values:
Together we love and respect. We are creative, we are determined, we are confident, we are kind are thoroughly embedded in all that the school does.
Our vision ‘Exploring and achieving as we grow together’ is the bedrock for every decision made at every level – from pupil interactions, teaching, to leadership and governance.
Our overarching aims are expressed under the following headings:
1. Distinctive Features, Overall Effectiveness, Culture, Vision and Values Aims
Our primary aim is for our Church of England school to be true to its vision of ‘exploring and achieving as we grow together’. For our family culture, where all members of our school community – children, staff, governors, parents and carers – are valued, included and supported. We have physically grown as a school to a one form entry, we continue to grow and develop as we support each other to achieve our aims, goals and aspirations.
2. Curriculum and Teaching Aims
To provide a curriculum that engages, excites, encourages creativity and curiosity and a deep love of learning.
To ensure teaching meets the needs of all children – is inclusive, adaptive and innovative; ensuring all children have the confidence, determination and experience they need to be successful.
3. Attendance and Behaviour / Personal Development and Wellbeing Aims
To ensure St Blaise is a happy, kind place, where everyone feels safe and welcomed through a nurturing environment. Where children develop socially and emotionally in a supportive and collaborative environment, working in partnership with parents and carers. An environment where love and respect are the foundation for actions and policies which support fairness and equality.
To provide an exceptional, play-based and outdoor-rich Early Years provision where children develop curiosity, independence, communication, and a love of learning through high-quality continuous and enhanced provision that builds strong foundations for future success.
5. Leadership and Governance Aims
To set the direction for our school, to be strategic, to be considerate of the specific needs of our school community. To hold the school’s vision and values uppermost when determining school policies. Whilst upholding high expectations of all, to be mindful of everyone’s wellbeing and mental health.
To facilitate strong and effective governance; a reflective governing body that provides support and challenge to drive improvement.
To maintain strong financial management practices and deliver the best value for money from the financial resources available to enable the school to achieve its strategic aims
We hope that you find the information and links informative. If you require any further information or would like to contact us, all governors can be contacted through the school office or email the Chair of Governors, Linda Shatford chair.3260@st-blaise.oxon.sch.uk. Your comments and suggestions are always welcomed; we would very much like to hear from you.
The Governing Body is appointed by Oxfordshire Local Authority

Breakfast club has been running successfully for six years. We have between 6-10 children each day with a current capacity of 15. Children can arrive from 8am and then go straight to registration in classes at the end.
Children have the choice of cereal, toast, or both. There is fruit juice, milk, and water available to drink. During each session children can play games, do art-based activities and spend time reading to staff. They have time to eat and plenty of time to talk to each other and those who care for them.
Children said, “I love eating cereal and toast”
“I like playing loads of games, running around and sitting at the table”
